title: Palmnut Soup with Selim Pods
author: Fafa Gilbert
desc: An Ewe cook's spice-forward palmnut soup — selim pods, dawadawa powder, African nutmeg and smoked paprika, with a kilo each of goat and smoked fish.
longDesc: This is the most aromatic documented palmnut soup and the only one by an Ewe cook, for whom the soup is dedetsi rather than abenkwan. It is built on a commercial concentrate let down with a litre and a half of warm water, and what makes it distinctive is the spicing: three selim pods, a tablespoon of dawadawa powder, a teaspoon of blended African nutmeg and a tablespoon of smoked paprika, alongside three tablespoons of shrimp powder. A kilo of goat, a kilo of assorted smoked fish, okra, garden eggs and mushrooms. The method is video-only, so only the quantities are published.
ingredients: 1 packet palmnut concentrate — packet weight not given
steps: // The published method for this recipe is video-only. No written steps exist in the source.
Let the palmnut concentrate down with the 1.5 litres of warm water and strain.
Cook the goat meat with the aromatics until tender.
Add the palm liquid and bring to a simmer.
Add the selim pods, dawadawa powder, African nutmeg, smoked paprika and shrimp powder.
Add the smoked fish, okra, garden eggs and mushrooms.
Simmer until the oil rises and the palm taste has cooked out.
// The order and timings above are inferred from the other documented palmnut soups, not from this source.
chefTips: Be aware that the method here is reconstructed. The source publishes a full ingredient list but its instructions are in a video, so the step order above follows the other documented palmnut soups rather than this cook's own sequence.
Selim pods — hwentia, Ethiopian pepper — are the signature of this soup. Bruise them and add them whole so they can be fished out; they are smoky and faintly bitter and nothing substitutes.
Dawadawa powder is fermented locust bean and it is the deepest savoury note available in West African cooking. A tablespoon is a lot, and it should be.
African nutmeg (calabash nutmeg, ehuru) is not nutmeg and tastes nothing like it. If you cannot get it, leave it out rather than substituting.
Three kinds of chilli — habanero, pettie belle and mild green — layered for aroma rather than heat alone. The pettie belle at 10 g is a small amount by weight.
Smoked paprika is the one non-traditional item in the list and the cook includes it deliberately; it reinforces the smoked fish.
This is an Ewe cook's version, where the soup is dedetsi. The Akan abenkwan versions at GHA019 and GHA020 are plainer.
commonMistakes: Treating the reconstructed step order as the author's own.
Grinding the selim pods into the soup so they cannot be removed.
Substituting ordinary nutmeg for African nutmeg.
Leaving out the dawadawa, which carries the savoury backbone.
Adding the okra early, so it disintegrates.
sources: Quantities from 'The Tastiest Ghanaian Palmnut Soup Recipe', byline as printed 'Fafa Gilbert', ndudu-by-fafa.blogspot.com, Saturday 19 May 2018. The recipe uses a commercial concentrate, 'EZ Palmnut', which the post credits to Barbara Mantey. Fafa Gilbert is Ewe, from the Volta Region, per her own site — the basis for the community attribution above.

Ingredients exactly as printed: 1 packet of EZ Palmnut (PACKET WEIGHT NOT GIVEN — a real gap, since it is the base of the soup); 1.5 litres of warm water; 3 large onions; 2 large tomatoes; 150g okra; 100g garden eggs; 3 habanero chillies; 10g pettie belle chillies; 3 selim pods; 3 tablespoons shrimp powder; 1 tablespoon dawadawa powder; 1 teaspoon blended African nutmeg; 1 tablespoon smoked paprika; 1kg goat meat; 1kg assorted smoked fish; 150g mushrooms.

METHOD GAP, stated plainly rather than disguised: NO WRITTEN METHOD AND NO DONENESS CUE exist in the source. The instructions are published as video only. The steps in this entry are explicitly marked as reconstructed from the other documented palmnut soups (GHA019, GHA020 and the KNUST standardised study), and the header comment in the step list says so. Nothing in the step order is attributed to this author.

THE PACKET WEIGHT OF THE CONCENTRATE IS NOT PRINTED, which means the single most important quantity in the recipe — how much palm base to 1.5 litres of water — is missing. No figure has been invented for it.

WHY IT IS PUBLISHED DESPITE THOSE GAPS: the spicing is documented nowhere else in the palmnut soup record. Selim pods, dawadawa powder and African nutmeg together are a distinctly Ewe treatment, and the quantities for all three are printed. The entry is published for the ingredient list, with its method honestly labelled as inferred.

ON THE SPICES: selim pods are Xylopia aethiopica, also called hwentia, grains of Selim or Ethiopian pepper. African nutmeg is Monodora myristica, also calabash nutmeg or ehuru, and is botanically unrelated to true nutmeg. Dawadawa is fermented Parkia biglobosa locust bean; its own fermentation is documented at GHA078.
SMOKED PAPRIKA is the one item with no West African provenance and is this cook's own addition, flagged rather than removed.
A fourth documented base for this soup, alongside fresh nuts, tinned cream and straight palm oil — see the sources at GHA019 for the full comparison.
reheating: Simmer gently. Remove the selim pods before storing or they turn the soup bitter.
healthBenefits: Palm fruit concentrate supplies provitamin-A carotenoids and tocotrienols.
Goat is leaner than beef or lamb.
Smoked fish adds omega-3 fats, protein and iodine.
Selim pods and African nutmeg both carry documented antimicrobial aromatic compounds.
culturalNote: The Ewe call this soup dedetsi and spice it far more heavily than Akan cooks do, which is the kind of regional difference that gets lost when a dish is published under one national name. Selim pods and dawadawa are the markers — smoky and fermented respectively, and both older in the regional kitchen than any of the chillies alongside them.
